rv.q: The sets and special effects are breathtaking, the costumes intricately designed and reimagined, the performances consistently some of the most sincere and moving of the season.
Regardless of my conflicted response, Christopher Donahue continues to charm as Scrooge, a role he reprises for a second season.

Opening Thursday for a holiday visit, this enjoyable family event is a restaged version of an Old Vic dramatization of Charles Dickens’ 1843 tale that played Broadway during the 2019-2020 season. Campbell Scott starred as Ebenezer Scrooge. Andrea Martin and LaChanze played featured roles.
Although it’s not a musical, the arrangements underscore the entire show, adding cinematic flair. Hugh Vanstone’s gothic lighting and Warchus’ frequent employment of dry ice also enhance the tale.
I wholeheartedly encourage audiences to experience this beloved Goodman holiday tradition - an annual production that never fails to capture the true spirit of the season.
This production is bigger and better than ever!
The Goodman Theatre, celebrating its 100th season, is once again the home for the most spectacular production of Charles Dickens' A Christmas Carole in Chicago and maybe anywhere.
There is simply no better way to welcome the holiday season than a visit to Goodman Theatre’s “A Christmas Carol.”
This is a delightful and handsomely mounted show with a spry, energetic cast.
I highly recommend that you get yourself and some friends over to the Goodman Theatre in Chicago's Loop for an excellent production that would charm the Grinch out of stealing Christmas.
This delightful holiday treat is a heartwarming experience that every family should embrace and treasure.

The Goodman staging of A Christmas Carol is an exciting and satisfying visual extravaganza that incorporates all manner of stagecraft with technologies old and new, while retaining the essential aspects of the original.
The fine acting, singing, and dancing make the presentation unique and fun for those of all ages.

cn.t: Goodman's 48th annual production earns strong praise for fresh direction and performances while honoring tradition. Critics laud Christopher Donahue's Scrooge and the show's balance of darkness and joy in this reimagined classic.
